title: Not Everyone Deserves Voting Rights
description:
Voting is not and was never meant to be a universal constitutional right. We break down the actual history,  from property requirements and literacy tests to what Washington, Franklin, and Adams actually said about who should have a say in how the country is run.

Plus: the Left's decades-long crusade to expand voting to non-citizens, felons, and people who contribute nothing, and what household voting could look like as a solution.

comments.text:
I agree with all of the voting requirements that Steven listed except for the one vote per household. There's no reason that two single people's votes should count for more than two married people. He also gives the example that a house divided cancels out the vote, but I feel like he's not considering that a strong marriage might produce double the vote. If a marriage is not in unity, maybe it's BETTER that the vote gets cancelled out, and if the marriage is strong then maybe their vote SHOULD be amplified. We should pursue encouraging stronger marriages rather than restricting their political influence, plus it's a really hard political point to sell. Why fight unnecessary battles and give free ammunition to the opposition? With that being said I also think that there is a risk with mail-in-ballots of a spouse in a divided household voting on behalf of their partner without their consent.

Additionally, just like there is no taxation without representation, there should be no representation without taxation. What if there was a cumulative tracker of how much taxes you have paid throughout your life and how many benefits you have received, then every year (or election cycle) that the cumulative benefits outweigh the cumulative paid, you don't get to vote that year. Heck, you could even make that a ratio rather than a 1-to-1 comparison, since the primary purpose of taxation is NOT FOR WELFARE, and taxation/welfare are not a zero-sum game.

I've also moved between states a few times over the past few years, and I've been surprised at how easy it is to register to vote at the state level when crossing state lines. Maybe there should be more guardrails on that to prevent cultural erosion during blue state migration and people poisoning primaries to game the system.
